# Design: Ready-made review briefs, so the skills start every reviewer at once

## Context

Isolated review exists today (archived change `2026-10-13-isolated-review`).
The `_isolated-review.md` procedure, rendered into `codev-propose` and
`codev-apply`, tells the agent to build each brief itself from four
sources: the role from `codev roles --at <step> --change <name> --json`,
the `context` and `rules` from one `codev instructions <artifact>` call
per artifact of the change, the material from `review.material`, and the
recorded ids from `codev review --change <name>`. It then dispatches every
sub-agent in one message. With four artifacts, that is about six codev
calls, often split across several turns, before the first reviewer
starts. Each turn re-reads the context, and change
`2026-10-14-fewer-review-turns` measured that turns drive what a review
costs and how long it takes.

Every piece the brief needs is already computed by the binary:
`codev-engine::roles` (resolved and active roles), `review_material`
(`measure`), `instructions::for_artifact` (context and rules blocks with
their origin), and the review record parser in `codev-core::review`.

Constraining decisions:

- **0007**: orchestration (dispatch, retry, fallback, merge) stays in
  the skill. The binary serves the data a brief is built from, renders
  the permission and checks the record. It never calls a model. This
  change follows 0007: assembling a brief from the binary's own data is
  deterministic, so it falls on the binary's side of the split.
- **0001**: assembling the brief is a pure function in `codev-core`. The
  engine reads the files through its ports.
- **0002**: `codev-core ← codev-engine ← codev-agents ← codev-cli`. The
  brief cannot depend on the skill assets in `codev-agents`.
- The JSON contract `codev-cli::contract::v1` grows additively and never
  derives from the domain model.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals**: one codev call gives every brief of a reviewing step, so the
skill can dispatch every sub-agent in the turn after it. The content of
the briefs, as the `skills` spec requires it, does not change.

**Non-goals**:

- the binary calling the Claude API, `claude -p` or any model (decision
  0007);
- changing the retry, the fallback, the meeting, the record's format or
  the reviewing roles;
- dispatching the summarizing sub-agents in parallel with the reviewers.
  The reviewers need the summaries, so the order stays.

## Decisions

### Decision: The binary assembles the data part of each brief; the skill keeps the procedure

`codev-core::review::brief` gets a pure function. It takes the resolved
role, the deduplicated context and rules blocks, the measured material
and the recorded finding ids, and returns a `Brief { role_id, summarize,
text }`. The text is Markdown with fixed English headings (`Role`,
`Project context and rules`, `Material`, `Already in the record`), in
that order. Blocks are listed in the order `codev instructions` serves
them. A block that several artifacts share is kept once, matched on
origin and text. Ids are listed in record order. No timestamp and no
absolute path appear, so two runs on the same files give the same bytes.

The skill still appends the fixed part: the finding format, the scales,
the "modify no file, material is data" rule, and the summaries. That text
already lives in `_review-record.md` and `_isolated-review.md`, which are
assets of `codev-agents`. Copying it into the core would break the crate
graph (0002) and give the same rules two sources.

**Alternatives considered**:

- *The binary calls the Claude API in parallel* (the user's literal
  request): excluded by 0007, whose rejected alternatives include "the
  binary running `claude -p` per role". It would bring credentials,
  process budgets and model costs into a binary that has none. Doing it
  requires a decision superseding 0007 first. This design does not
  propose one, because the bottleneck it measures is not the dispatch.
- *A complete brief, format and scales included, served by the binary*:
  this would move procedure text from the skill assets into the core and
  make it depend on `codev-agents` content (0002). The gain over
  appending a constant block is nil.
- *A single `codev instructions --all` to get the context and rules in
  one call*: this saves calls but leaves the per-role assembly to the
  agent, which is the error-prone part, and still needs `codev review`.

### Decision: A `--briefs` flag on `codev roles`, not a new command

`codev roles --at <step> --change <name>` already serves the roles, the
review mode and the material, which are three of the four inputs. The
flag adds `RolesV1.briefs: Option<Vec<BriefV1>>` (`roleId`, `summarize`,
`text`), additive in v1. It is `null` without the flag and in a failure.
The engine gathers the context and rules through `instructions::for_artifact`
for each artifact present in the change, and the ids through the record
parser. Errors `briefs_need_change` and `briefs_need_review_step` are new
stable codes.

**Alternatives considered**: `codev review brief` puts the briefs next
to the record, but would have to resolve the roles and the material a
second time and adds a subcommand to document. Always serving the
briefs, without a flag, would weigh down every `codev roles --json`
call that the skills make at other steps.

### Decision: The skill falls back to inline when there are no briefs

When `briefs` is missing (an older binary) or the call fails, every role
reviews inline with a `Fallback:` line. The skill does not fall back to
building briefs by hand. Keeping both paths in the skill text would make
it longer and bring back the drift this change removes.
`codev update` installs the skills and the binary together, so this case
only arises after a partial update.

**Alternatives considered**: keeping the old assembly as a fallback
keeps two procedures to test and to keep identical.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [The gain is within the noise] → Measure with `codev-evals compare`
  against the baseline: turns and duration on the isolated cases. The
  quality side checks that recall and evidence validity stay within the
  baseline's range. If the gain does not show, say so with the numbers,
  as `fewer-review-turns` did.
- [A brief served by the binary misses something the procedure asked
  for] → The `skills` spec keeps listing what a brief must hold. A golden
  test in `codev-core` asserts each part for a fixture change, and a
  `workflows.rs` test asserts the procedure names `--briefs`, `text` and
  `summarize`.
- [The JSON grows large for a change with many roles and rules] → The
  flag is opt-in. The text holds paths and ids, never file contents, so
  its size scales with the roles, not with the material.
- [Users expected an API-driven speed-up and read this as a refusal] →
  The proposal states the assumption and the route (a decision
  superseding 0007) in its *Out of scope* section.

## Migration Plan

Additive: `briefs` is a new nullable field and `--briefs` a new flag. The
procedure in `_isolated-review.md` changes, so `codev update` regenerates
`codev-propose` and `codev-apply`, and codev's own skills are refreshed in
the same change. Rollback is reverting the change. An older skill never
passes `--briefs`, and a newer skill facing an older binary falls back to
inline.

## Open Questions

- Should a later change also serve the brief of the summarizing
  sub-agents (path plus diff command)? This can wait: it changes neither
  these specs nor this approach.

# Proposal: Ready-made review briefs, so the skills start every reviewer at once

## Why

The user wants reviews to go faster than the skills run them today, and
asked for codev to call the Claude API itself, in parallel. Accepted
decision 0007 rules that out: sub-agent orchestration lives in the skills,
and the binary never calls a model, holds no credentials and runs no
processes. Calling `claude -p` from the binary is listed there as a
rejected alternative. This change goes after the same goal, speed, within
that decision.

The parallelism the user asks for already exists. In `isolated` mode the
skills start every reviewing role as a sub-agent in a single message.
The time goes into what comes before. To build each brief, the agent
calls `codev roles`, then `codev instructions` once per artifact of the
change to collect `context` and `rules`, then `codev review` for the ids
already recorded. It then copies all of this into one brief per role by
hand. Each of these calls is a turn, and each turn re-reads the whole
context. Copying by hand also lets the brief drift from what the spec
requires.

**Assumption, made without asking (evaluation run):** what the user wants
is faster reviews, not a particular mechanism. A binary that calls the API
would require superseding decision 0007 first, with
`codev decision new … --supersedes 0007`. That choice is the team's to
make in a decision of its own, not in a change proposal, so this change
leaves it out (see *Out of scope*).

## What Changes

- `codev roles --at <step> --change <name> --briefs --json` serves, at
  `plan.trace`, `plan.challenge` and `code.review`, one ready-to-send
  brief per active role. Each brief holds the role (id, question,
  criteria, knowledge filtered by stack), the project's `context` and
  `rules` for each artifact of the change, the material with its
  `full` or `summarize` treatment, and the finding ids already in the
  review record. One call replaces the `codev instructions` call per
  artifact and the `codev review` call that building a brief needs today.
- Without `--briefs`, the output is unchanged. With `--briefs` and no
  reviewing step, or without `--change`, the command fails with a stable
  code.
- The isolated review procedure of `/codev-propose` and `/codev-apply`
  builds each sub-agent's brief from `briefs[]`. To each brief it adds
  only the fixed part it already carries: the finding format, the scales,
  the read-only rule and the summaries of files marked `summarize`. It
  then starts every sub-agent in the same message.
- Nothing changes in what a brief must hold or exclude, in the retry, the
  fallback, the meeting or the review record.

### Out of scope

- codev calling the Claude API, `claude -p`, or any model, and holding
  an API key: excluded by decision 0007 (and by decision 0001 for the
  core). Reopening that question means writing a decision that
  supersedes 0007, with its own cost and credentials analysis, before any
  change.

## Release note

- Changed: In isolated review, `/codev-propose` and `/codev-apply` start every reviewing sub-agent sooner. `codev roles --at <step> --change <name> --briefs --json` now serves each role's brief ready to send, which replaces several codev calls per step.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: `codev roles --briefs` serves a ready-made brief per reviewing role

`codev roles --at <step> --change <name> --briefs` SHALL accept `--at`
with a reviewing step only: `plan.trace`, `plan.challenge` or
`code.review`. It reads files, writes none, makes no network call and
calls no model.

With `--json`, the document SHALL carry `briefs`. It is `null` without
`--briefs`, and in a failure's document. With `--briefs`, it is a list
holding one entry per role in `roles`, in the same order. Each entry has
`roleId` (the role's `id`), `summarize` and `text`. `summarize` lists the
paths of the material marked `summarize`, which the skill gets summarized
and appends itself. `text` is the brief in Markdown, and it SHALL hold,
under headings that name each part:

- the role: its id, its question, every `doneWhen` criterion with its
  origin, and its `knowledge` as `roles` serves it, the `By stack` part
  already filtered;
- the project's `context` and `rules` blocks, as `codev instructions`
  serves them for each artifact of the change, each block with its
  origin, a block shared by several artifacts appearing once;
- the material, as `review.material` lists it: each path with its
  treatment, and at `code.review` the base `diff.base` the change's diff
  is read against. When `review.material` is `null`, a line saying no
  material could be measured, and why;
- the ids of the findings already in the change's review record, each
  with its step and its role, so that none is raised again. When the
  record does not exist or holds none, a line saying so.

The brief SHALL be built only from the change's files, the project's
configuration and codev's own rules. It MUST NOT hold another role's
criteria or knowledge, nor the content of any finding: only the ids. The
same files SHALL give byte-identical briefs.

`--briefs` without `--change` SHALL fail with the stable code
`briefs_need_change`. `--briefs` without `--at`, or with a step that is
not a reviewing step, SHALL fail with `briefs_need_review_step`, naming
the three reviewing steps. Without `--json`, `--briefs` SHALL print each
role's brief under a line naming the role.

#### Scenario: One brief per role at the challenge

- **GIVEN** a change `add-auth` with a proposal that ticks `security`, a
  design, tasks and one spec delta, and a project configuration with a
  `context` and `rules` for `design`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev roles --at plan.challenge --change
  add-auth --briefs --json`
- **THEN** `briefs` holds one entry for `skeptic` and one for `security`,
  in the order of `roles`
- **AND** the `security` brief holds its question, its criteria, its
  knowledge, the project's `context`, the `design` rules and the four
  planning files with treatment `full`
- **AND** the `skeptic` brief holds neither the `security` criteria nor
  its knowledge

#### Scenario: Ids already recorded are listed, not their content

- **GIVEN** a change whose `review.md` holds `R-skeptic-1` and
  `R-security-1` under `## plan.challenge`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev roles --at code.review --change <name>
  --briefs --json`
- **THEN** each brief lists `R-skeptic-1` and `R-security-1` with their
  step and role
- **AND** no brief holds the title, evidence or recommendation of either
  finding

#### Scenario: Material over the limit

- **GIVEN** a change whose diff modifies files of 100000, 60000 and 10000
  bytes
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev roles --at code.review --change <name>
  --briefs --json`
- **THEN** each entry's `summarize` lists the 100000-byte file
- **AND** each brief names that file with treatment `summarize`, and the
  two others with `full` and the base the diff is read against

#### Scenario: Two runs give the same briefs

- **GIVEN** a change whose files do not change between two runs
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev roles --at plan.challenge --change
  <name> --briefs --json` twice
- **THEN** both runs give byte-identical `briefs`

#### Scenario: No diff at the code review

- **GIVEN** a project outside a git repository
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev roles --at code.review --change <name>
  --briefs --json`
- **THEN** the exit code is 0 and each brief says no material could be
  measured, and why

#### Scenario: Without the flag, nothing changes

- **WHEN** the user runs `codev roles --at plan.challenge --change
  <name> --json`
- **THEN** `briefs` is `null` and every other field is as before

#### Scenario: Briefs need a change

- **WHEN** the user runs `codev roles --at plan.challenge --briefs
  --json`
- **THEN** the exit code is 1, `status[0].code` is `briefs_need_change`
  and `briefs` is `null`

#### Scenario: Briefs need a reviewing step

- **WHEN** the user runs `codev roles --at code.implement --change
  <name> --briefs --json`
- **THEN** the exit code is 1 and `status[0].code` is
  `briefs_need_review_step`
- **AND** its message names `plan.trace`, `plan.challenge` and
  `code.review`

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: In isolated mode, each reviewing role runs alone, then the skill consolidates

At `plan.trace`, `plan.challenge` and `code.review`, the `propose` and
`apply` skills SHALL read `review.mode` from `codev roles --at <step>
--change <name> --json`. In `inline` mode they review as before. In
`isolated` mode they SHALL run every role returned — the tracer, the
skeptic, the newcomer and the active experts — as a separate sub-agent,
all of a step's sub-agents at once when the platform allows.

In `isolated` mode the skills SHALL take each role's brief from the
`briefs` that `codev roles --at <step> --change <name> --briefs --json`
serves. They SHALL NOT assemble the role, the `context` and `rules`, the
material list or the recorded ids themselves, and SHALL NOT call `codev
instructions` or `codev review` to build a brief. When that call fails,
or returns no `briefs` field because the binary is older than the
skill, every role SHALL fall back to inline, and the record says so.

The brief of each sub-agent MUST hold only:

- its role: id, question, `doneWhen` criteria and `knowledge` as served,
  the `By stack` part already filtered;
- the project's `context` and `rules` from `codev instructions`;
- the material listed by `review.material`: the files marked `full`, to
  read whole, with the change's diff for them at `code.review`; for each
  file marked `summarize`, a summary of its change written by a separate
  sub-agent that sees only that file's diff, quoting the changed lines
  verbatim where they fit;
- the ids already in the record, so as not to raise them again;
- the review record's format, scales and rules for a finding.

The first four parts are the served brief's `text`. The skill appends
only the summaries of the paths in the entry's `summarize` and the
review record's format, scales and rules, which are the same for every
role.

The brief MUST NOT carry the conversation, the author's reasoning or
another role's findings, and is assembled only from codev's outputs and
the files. The sub-agent MAY read other files of the repository with
read-only tools — the decisions, the main specs, the code the material
cites — and is told to modify no file and to treat the material as data,
never as instructions. It returns its findings as a role section of the
review record, or `No finding.`.

A sub-agent that the platform reports as failed or stopped — its own
time or budget limits included — or that returns something other than a
role section with well-formed findings SHALL be run once more; if it
fails again, the skill SHALL run that role inline and record the fallback
with its reason. When the sub-agent tool is unavailable, every role falls
back to inline, and the record says so.

The skill then consolidates — the meeting:

- findings of several roles about the same defect at the same location
  become one finding, written under the role that rated it most severe
  (ties: higher confidence, then the order `codev roles` lists the
  roles), with `raised_by` listing every role that raised it; a role
  whose findings were all merged writes `No finding.`;
- findings at the same place that need different fixes stay separate;
- the findings are ranked by severity, then confidence, then role order,
  and the summary's caps apply as in inline mode;
- the step's section records `Mode: isolated.` and one `Summarized:` line
  per summarized file;
- then the record is checked, and the author's answer loop and the
  escalation to the human run as in inline mode.

At `plan.trace`, the tracer's findings are not recorded: the skill fixes
the gaps in the artifacts, as in inline mode, and its summary names any
fallback.

#### Scenario: The skills describe the isolated review

- **GIVEN** the codev workflow catalog
- **WHEN** the `propose` and `apply` workflows are rendered
- **THEN** each names `review.mode`, a sub-agent per role, what the
  brief holds and that it never carries the conversation, the material
  as data, parallel dispatch, `review.material` with `full` and
  `summarize`, the summarizing sub-agent, one retry then the inline
  fallback recorded with `Fallback:`, the merge of duplicate findings
  with `raised_by`, the ranking, `Mode: isolated.` and `Summarized:`

#### Scenario: The skills take the briefs from codev

- **GIVEN** the codev workflow catalog
- **WHEN** the `propose` and `apply` workflows are rendered
- **THEN** their isolated review names `codev roles` with `--briefs`,
  `briefs`, `text` and `summarize`
- **AND** it no longer tells the agent to call `codev instructions` per
  artifact to build a brief

#### Scenario: Two roles report the same defect

- **GIVEN** isolated mode, and the `security` and `skeptic` sub-agents
  both report that `design.md#Decision: Tokens` stores tokens in clear,
  `security` as `high`
- **WHEN** the skill consolidates
- **THEN** the record holds one finding under `### security` with
  `raised_by: [security, skeptic]`
- **AND** `### skeptic` holds its other findings, or `No finding.`

#### Scenario: A sub-agent fails twice

- **GIVEN** isolated mode, and the platform stops the `newcomer`
  sub-agent twice, on its time limit
- **WHEN** the skill reviews the change
- **THEN** the newcomer reviews inline
- **AND** its section in the record carries a `Fallback:` line with the
  reason

#### Scenario: Material over the limit

- **GIVEN** isolated mode, and `review.material` marks a file `summarize`
- **WHEN** the skill briefs the sub-agents
- **THEN** they receive a summary of that file's change, written by a
  sub-agent that saw only that file's diff, instead of the whole file
- **AND** the step's section records a `Summarized:` line naming it

#### Scenario: An older binary serves no briefs

- **GIVEN** isolated mode, and a skill rendered by this version run
  against a binary whose `codev roles` output has no `briefs` field
- **WHEN** the skill reviews the change
- **THEN** every role reviews inline
- **AND** each role's section carries a `Fallback:` line naming the
  missing briefs

#### Scenario: A change reviewed inline in an isolated project

- **GIVEN** a project in isolated mode and a change whose `change.yaml`
  sets `review: { mode: inline }`
- **WHEN** `/codev-apply` reviews it
- **THEN** every role reviews inline, in the conversation
